propositions: The close gate's undeclared-paths refusal message instructs authors to declare new paths and retry, but declaring them changes the file_impact hash which triggers stale-material rejection on retry.
Widening file_impact retroactively broadens what an existing attestation signature claims to cover, because the signature scope is built from file_impact union cited files.
The undeclared-paths refusal message must explicitly state that declaring new paths is a material plan change and that rebar review-plan must be re-run before close can succeed.

The materiality check hashes the entire file_impact list wholesale, so any mutation including purely additive changes are equally detectable as stale, with no residue distinguishing removal from addition.
Both gates fire correctly under their current conditions and must continue firing identically; only the first gate's message requires clarification to set correct expectations.
